episode_title: Stop Being Available: How to Set Better Boundaries and Take Your Power Back

real_qa.q: What did Dr. Eric Thomas realize about his wife Didi's sacrifice when she was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis?
real_qa.r: Dr. Thomas realized that while he was traveling the world chasing his dreams and goals, Didi was carrying the entire load at home—making sure bills were paid, health benefits were maintained, and the foundation was stable. When Didi was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, he understood that the stress she was bearing because of his dreams was a contributing factor, and he recognized he had to protect her from the new roles and traveling schedules he was taking on without consulting her.
real_qa.requete: Eric Thomas wife Didi multiple sclerosis stress

real_qa.q: How should women who fear disappointing their family by stopping caregiving duties respond, according to Dr. Eric Thomas?
real_qa.r: Dr. Thomas tells women that family members will be disappointed initially, but they will be empowered to step up and learn. He gives his own example: when Didi stopped handling all the bills, he had to start doing them and he didn't die. He emphasizes that by stepping back from the role, family members are given an opportunity to take responsibility, and they will ultimately become a bigger blessing to the woman than she ever was to them.
real_qa.requete: women stop caregiving disappoint family step up

real_qa.q: What principle should guide women's decision-making when deciding what responsibilities to keep, according to Dr. Eric Thomas?
real_qa.r: Dr. Thomas advises women to get out of their feelings and get into principles. The key principle is: are you the best person for the job? If you're not training somebody else to do something well, that's a problem because you'll have to do it for the rest of your life, making it overwhelming. Everything you do well, you must teach somebody else because you cannot be a mother the same way for the rest of your life—at some point, family members need to grow up and there needs to be reciprocity.
real_qa.requete: best person for the job principle responsibility

real_qa.q: What does Dr. Eric Thomas say about the importance of identity beyond roles like motherhood or partnership?
real_qa.r: Dr. Thomas emphasizes that you are more than a role and bigger than what you do. Before you became a mother or wife, you were somebody—that's why they chose you. Your family loves you because of who you are, not what you do. Even if you weren't a wife, partner, speaker, counselor, or coach, you would still be special and your voice and gifts matter independently of any role.
real_qa.requete: identity beyond role motherhood wife value person

real_qa.q: What specific changes did Dr. Eric Thomas and Didi make to their daily communication and relationship after recognizing the burden she was carrying?
real_qa.r: Dr. Thomas committed to giving Didi a voice in decisions and listening to her. They now talk every morning from 7:30 to 8:30 a.m. where he listens. Didi expressed she wanted his undivided attention when shopping, dining, or spending time together as a family—not him being on his phone or taking calls. She also wanted him to be present at the fitting room and genuinely pay attention to her, rather than just being physically present.
real_qa.requete: Eric Thomas Didi daily communication 7:30 listening
